title: Crystal Palace 2-1 Real Sociedad: McNeil completes turnaround as Frank earns first win
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutCrystal Palace 2-1 Real Sociedad: McNeil completes turnaround as Frank earns first winShareAfter starting his tenure with a dispiriting defeat to Coventry City, Thomas Frank oversaw his first win as Crystal Palace's head coach.Thomas Frank earned his first victory in charge of Crystal Palace as his side came from behind to beat 10-man Real Sociedad 2-1 in the Conference League.
It looked as though Frank would suffer a second defeat in as many games with the Eagles when Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr gave La Real a deserved lead in the 66th minute.

However, Jon Martin's second yellow card gave Palace a numerical advantage only five minutes later, and after Jean-Philippe Mateta's penalty drew them level, Dwight McNeil's predatory finish completed the fightback.
Palace even had a chance to add some gloss when they were awarded a second penalty in stoppage time, but with Mateta having been substituted, Yeremy Pino stepped up and was thwarted by Unai Marrero.
Clear-cut chances were few and far between in the first half, with the best of them falling to La Real's Goncalo Guedes, who saw his first-time effort repelled by Dean Henderson 36 minutes in.
Guedes was the provider when Mikel Oyarzabal squandered an even better opportunity early in the second half, with the World Cup winner shooting straight at Henderson from a glorious position.
The visitors did go in front soon afterwards, though, with Sarr marking his return to London with a sweeping finish from Job Ochieng's right-wing centre.

But the momentum completely switched when Martin – who had earlier been booked for catching Pino with his hand – dragged Mateta down inside the box. The Palace striker dusted himself down to convert from 12 yards, and the hosts looked a team transformed from that moment on.
The decisive moment came with 81 minutes gone, as substitute Jorgen Strand Larsen saw an attempted bicycle kick squirm across the six-yard box, leaving McNeil to apply an easy finish.
A blatant handball from Carlos Soler to block McNeil's shot later gave Palace another spot-kick, and Marrero's save from Pino almost led to La Real snatching a point.

Substitute Orri Oskarsson broke down the right-hand channel six minutes into added time, only for Henderson to turn his strike onto the outside of the post, and Sarr nodded over from the resulting corner as the visitors ran out of time.
Frank maintains European feel-good factor
In the Premier League, with Palace having just seven points on the board and propping up the table, there has been little positivity around Selhurst Park.

But things have been very different in Europe, with Thursday's victory extending Palace's unbeaten run in major UEFA competitions to nine home matches (W6 D3), since a 1-0 loss to AEK Larnaca in the Conference League in October 2025.

Frank's side had to ride their luck somewhat in the first half, with La Real winning the expected goals (xG) battle by 1.2 to 0.35 and out-shooting their opponents by 10 to four in the first period. Palace had not even registered an attempt on target by the interval.
But, boosted significantly by the award of two penalties, Palace ultimately won the xG battle by 4.57 to 2.73, including a figure of 2.53 open-play xG to La Real's 1.74.
Real Sociedad have now won just one of their 12 European games against English clubs (D3 L8), beating Manchester United 1-0 at Old Trafford in September 2022.
